content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the absorption of delafloxacin in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract by cation binding. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 2. Deferoxamine chelates iron, but its affinity for other minerals is unknown. Caution should be exercised, and close monitoring is necessary when used with aluminum hydroxide. 3. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of demeclocycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is advised to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, separate the doses by at least 2 hours. 4. Devil's claw reduces the effects of aluminum hydroxide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 5. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of dextroamphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 6. Aluminum hydroxide may increase the levels of diflunisal due to passive renal tubular reabsorption caused by an increase in urinary pH. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 7. Aluminum hydroxide increases salicylate levels at moderate doses but decreases them at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. Close monitoring is advised. 8. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of digoxin by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is necessary. 9. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of dolutegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after medications containing polyvalent cations. If possible, use alternative therapy. Close monitoring is required. 10. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, separate the doses by at least 2 hours. 11. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of eltrombopag by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. This combination is contraindicated. If co-administration is unavoidable, separate the doses by at least 4 hours. 12. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of elvitegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Elvitegravir plasma concentrations are reduced when co-administered with antacids due to ionic complex formation in the GI tract, not due to changes in gastric pH. Separate the administration of elvitegravir and antacids by at least 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. 13. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate the administration of antacids and this combination therapy by at least 2 hours. 14. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of enalapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 15. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of ephedrine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 16. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of erythromycin base, erythromycin ethylsuccinate, erythromycin lactobionate, and erythromycin stearate through an unknown mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 17. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of esmolol by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Separate the doses by at least 2 hours. 18. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of ethambutol by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid administering aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids for at least 4 hours following an ethambutol dose. Close monitoring is recommended. 19. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of etidronate by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Separate the doses by at least 2 hours. 20. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary.
